A.text: A particle starts from the origin at t = 0 with an initial velocity of 3.0 i m/s and moves in the x-y plane with a constant acceleration (6.0 i + 4.0 j) m/s^2. The x-coordinate of the particle at the instant when its y-coordinate is 32 m is D metres. The value of D is -
A.sol_text:
Given:
Initial velocity: vector u = 3 i m/s
Acceleration: vector a = 6 i + 4 j m/s^2
Y-coordinate when x-coordinate is D: y = 32 m

Using the equation of motion:
vector S = vector u t + (1/2) vector a t^2

For x-coordinate:
x = 3t + (1/2) × 6 t^2
x = 3t + 3t^2 .... (1)

For y-coordinate:
y = (1/2) × 4 × t^2 = 2t^2 = 32 (Given)

From y = 2t^2 = 32:
t^2 = 16
t = 4 sec .... (2)

Substituting t = 4 sec in equation (1):
x = 3 × 4 + 3 × 4^2
x = 12 + 3 × 16
x = 12 + 48
x = 60 m

Therefore, D = 60 metres

A.text: An electron of mass m and magnitude of charge |e| initially at rest gets accelerated by a constant electric field E. The rate of change of de-Broglie wavelength of this electron at time t ignoring relativistic effects is -

F = |e| E

V = at = |e| E t / m

d(lambda)/dt = h * d/dt[1 / (|e| Et)]

A.text: Two identical capacitors A and B, charged to the same potential 5V are connected in two different circuits as shown below at time t = 0. If the charge on capacitors A and B at time t = CR is Q_A and Q_B respectively, then (Here e is the base of natural logarithm)
A.sol_text:
For Circuit 1 (with diode):
The diode prevents the capacitor from discharging. Once charged to 5V, the capacitor A cannot discharge through the resistor. Therefore, the charge remains constant.
At t = CR: Q_A = CV (initial charge, no discharge)

For Circuit 2 (with capacitor only):
The capacitor B discharges through the resistor R following the RC discharge equation.
For discharging: Q(t) = Q_0 * e^(-t/RC)

At t = CR:
Q_B = Q_0 * e^(-CR/CR) = Q_0 * e^(-1) = (CV)/e

Therefore:
Q_A = VC
Q_B = VC/e

A.text: A wire of length L and mass per unit length 6.0 × 10^(-3) kg m^(-1) is put under tension of 540 N. Two consecutive frequencies that it resonates at are: 420 Hz and 490 Hz. Then L in meters is -
A.sol_text:
V = sqrt(T/mu) = sqrt(540/(6×10^(-3))) = sqrt(90000) = 300 m/s

For a wire fixed at both ends, resonance occurs at frequencies:
f_n = n × V/(2L)

Two consecutive resonant frequencies are 420 Hz and 490 Hz.
The difference between consecutive frequencies is:
Δf = f_(n+1) - f_n = V/(2L) = 490 - 420 = 70 Hz

Therefore:
V/(2L) = 70

⟹ L = V/(2 × 70) = 300/(2 × 70) = 300/140 = 2.1 m

A.text: A plane electromagnetic wave is propagating along the direction (i + j)/sqrt(2), with its polarization along the direction k. The correct form of the magnetic field of the wave would be (here B_0 is an appropriate constant)
A.sol_text:
Wave propagates in the direction of vector E × vector B.

Given: E is along k and wave propagates along (i + j)/sqrt(2)

Check: B = (i - j)/sqrt(2)

vector E × vector B = k × ((i - j)/sqrt(2)) = (i + j)/sqrt(2)

Since the electric field is along k (polarization direction) and the wave propagates along (i + j)/sqrt(2), the magnetic field must be perpendicular to both.

Using the right-hand rule: k × (i - j)/sqrt(2) = (i + j)/sqrt(2), which gives the propagation direction.

Therefore, the magnetic field must be of the form:
B = B_0 (i - j)/sqrt(2) cos(omega*t - k*(i + j)/sqrt(2))

This matches option (4).

A.text: A uniformly thick wheel with moment of inertia I and radius R is free to rotate about its centre of mass (see fig.). A massless string is wrapped over its rim and two blocks of masses m1 and m2 (m1 > m2) are attached to the ends of the string. The system is released from rest. The angular speed of the wheel when m1 descends by a distance h is -
A.sol_text:
By conservation of energy:
Loss in energy = Gain in energy

m1*g*h = m2*g*h + (1/2)*m1*V^2 + (1/2)*m2*V^2 + (1/2)*I*omega^2

(m1 - m2)*g*h = (1/2)*(m1 + m2)*V^2 + (1/2)*I*omega^2

Since V = R*omega (string does not slip on rim):
= (1/2)*(m1 + m2)*R^2*omega^2 + (1/2)*I*omega^2

= (1/2)*[I + (m1 + m2)*R^2]*omega^2

omega^2 = 2(m1 - m2)*g*h / [I + (m1 + m2)*R^2]

=> omega = [2(m1 - m2)*g*h / (I + (m1 + m2)*R^2)]^(1/2)

A.text: A particle of mass m is projected with a speed u from the ground at an angle theta = pi/3 w.r.t. horizontal (x-axis). When it has reached its maximum height, it collides completely inelastically with another particle of the same mass and velocity u i. The horizontal distance covered by the combined mass before reaching the ground is -
A.sol_text:
mu + mu*cos(theta) = 2mV
V = (u + u*cos(theta))/2
= (u + u*(1/2))/2
= (3u)/4

H_max = (u^2*sin^2(60°))/(2g) = (u^2*(3/4))/(2g) = (3u^2)/(8g)

Time taken = sqrt(2*H_max/g) = sqrt(2/g * (3u^2)/(8g)) = sqrt(3)*u/(2*g)

Horizontal distance travelled = (3u)/4 * (sqrt(3)*u)/(2*g) = (3*sqrt(3)*u^2)/(8*g)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A small spherical droplet of density d is floating exactly half immersed in a liquid of density ρ and surface tension T. The radius of the droplet is (take note that the surface tension applies an upward force on the droplet)
A.sol_text:
For a spherical droplet floating exactly half immersed in a liquid:

Forces acting on the droplet:
1. Weight of droplet: W = (4/3)πR³dg (downward)
2. Buoyant force: F_b = (2/3)πR³ρg (upward, from displaced liquid)
3. Surface tension force: F_s = 2πR·T (upward, acts along the contact line)

At equilibrium (half immersed):
T·2πR + (2/3)πR³ρg = (4/3)πR³dg

Simplifying:
T·2πR = (4/3)πR³dg - (2/3)πR³ρg

T·2πR = (2/3)πR³(2d - ρ)g

Dividing both sides by πR:
2T = (2/3)R²(2d - ρ)g

Solving for R²:
R² = 3T/(g(2d - ρ))

Therefore:
R = sqrt(3T/(g(2d - ρ)))

B.text: In a Young's double slit experiment 15 fringes are observed on a small portion of the screen when light of wavelength 500 nm is used. Ten fringes are observed on the same section of the screen when another light source of wavelength lambda is used. Then the value of lambda is (in nm).
B.sol_text:
For Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is given by:
beta = lambda * D / d

where D is the distance from slits to screen and d is the separation between slits.

For a fixed portion of the screen, the number of fringes observed is inversely proportional to the fringe width.

For the first wavelength (500 nm): 15 fringes are observed
For the second wavelength (lambda): 10 fringes are observed

Since the same section of the screen is considered:
N_1 * beta_1 = N_2 * beta_2

15 * 500 * (D/d) = 10 * lambda * (D/d)

The D/d terms cancel out:
15 * 500 = 10 * lambda

lambda = (15 * 500) / 10 = 7500 / 10 = 750 nm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In a meter bridge experiment S is a standard resistance. R is a resistance wire. It is found that balancing length is ℓ = 25 cm. If R is replaced by a wire of half length and half diameter that of R of same material, then the balancing distance ℓ' (in cm) will now be ..................
B.sol_text:
For the meter bridge, at balance:
X/R = ℓ/(100 - ℓ)

Initially with R:
X/R = 25/75 = 1/3

For resistance R:
R = ρL/A = ρℓ/(πd²/4) = 4ρℓ/(πd²)

When R is replaced by a wire of half length (ℓ/2) and half diameter (d/2) of same material:
R' = 4ρ(ℓ/2)/(π(d/2)²) = 4ρ(ℓ/2)/(π·d²/4) = 4ρ(ℓ/2)·4/(πd²) = (8ρℓ)/(πd²) = 2·(4ρℓ)/(πd²) = 2R

Now at balance:
X/R' = ℓ'/(100 - ℓ')

Since X and S remain same:
X/R' = (100 - ℓ')/ℓ'

(100 - ℓ')/ℓ' = X/(2R) = (1/2)·(X/R) = (1/2)·3 = 3/2

⟹ (100 - ℓ')/ℓ' = 3/2

⟹ 2(100 - ℓ') = 3ℓ'

⟹ 200 - 2ℓ' = 3ℓ'

⟹ 200 = 5ℓ'

⟹ [ℓ' = 40 cm]
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Amongst the following, the form of water with the lowest ionic conductance at 298 K is :
options: saline water used for intravenous injection
A.sol_text:
The form of H2O with the lowest ionic conductance at 298 K is distilled water.

Explanation: Ionic conductance depends on the number of ions present in the solution. 
- Sea water contains dissolved salts and minerals (NaCl, MgCl2, etc.), so it has high ionic conductance.
- Saline water used for intravenous injection is a solution of NaCl in water, so it contains ions and has ionic conductance.
- Water from a well contains dissolved minerals and salts from the ground, so it has ionic conductance.
- Distilled water is pure H2O obtained by distillation process, which removes all dissolved salts and minerals. It contains the minimum number of ions (only H+ and OH- from self-ionization of water, which is very negligible).

Therefore, distilled water has the lowest ionic conductance among all the given options.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which polymer has 'chiral' monomer(s) ?
A.sol_text:
PHBV : -[O-CH-CH2-C-O-CH-CH2-C-]n with CH3 below first CH, O double bonded, C2H5 below second CH, O double bonded

Monomer : CH3-*CH-CH2-COOH with OH below the starred carbon (3-Hydroxybutanoic acid) and CH3-CH2-*CH-CH2-COOH with OH below the starred carbon (3-Hydroxypentanoic acid)

Both monomers contain a chiral carbon atom (marked with *) as they have four different groups attached to them:
- 3-Hydroxybutanoic acid: The carbon bearing OH group is attached to CH3, H, OH, and CH2COOH (four different groups)
- 3-Hydroxypentanoic acid: The carbon bearing OH group is attached to CH3, CH2, H, OH, and CH2COOH (four different groups)

Nylon 6,6 is made from hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid - no chiral centers.
Neoprene is a synthetic rubber (polychloroprene) - no chiral centers in the monomer.
Buna-N is a copolymer of butadiene and acrylonitrile - no chiral centers in the monomers.

Therefore, PHBV is the only polymer with chiral monomers.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A mixture of gases O2, H2 and CO are taken in a closed vessel containing charcoal. The graph that represents the correct behaviour of pressure with time is:
options: Pressure decreasing with time (curved, approaching zero)
A.sol_text:
When a mixture of gases O2, H2 and CO are taken in a closed vessel containing charcoal, the charcoal will react with these gases through various reactions:

1. Charcoal reacts with O2: C + O2 → CO2
2. Charcoal reacts with H2: C + H2 → CH4 (or other hydrocarbons)
3. CO can react with charcoal under certain conditions

As these reactions proceed, the total number of moles of gas in the system decreases because:
- O2 is consumed (2 moles reactants → products)
- H2 is consumed
- The products formed may dissolve or condense

Since the vessel is closed and the volume is constant, by the ideal gas law (PV = nRT), as the number of moles (n) decreases while V and T remain constant, the pressure must decrease.

The pressure decreases gradually over time as the reactions continue. Initially, the pressure decreases rapidly when reactants are abundant, but as reactants get consumed, the reaction rate slows down. Eventually, the pressure approaches a constant value (or nearly constant) when the reaction essentially stops.

This behavior is best represented by option (4), which shows pressure decreasing with time in a curved manner (following first-order kinetics or similar) and eventually leveling off.

on increasing time, pressure will be decreases.

A.text: The true statement amongst the following is:
options: S is a function of temperature but ΔS is not a function of temperature.
Both ΔS and S are functions of temperature.
S is not a function of temperature but ΔS is a function of temperature.
Both S and ΔS are not functions of temperature.
A.sol_text:
S = ∫ dq/T

ΔS = nC ∫[T_i to T_f] dT/T

From the definition of entropy S, we can see that S is derived from integrating dq/T, which depends on the heat transfer at different temperatures. Therefore, S is a function of temperature.

From the expression for change in entropy ΔS, we have:
ΔS = nC ∫[T_i to T_f] dT/T

This clearly shows that ΔS depends on the temperature range (from T_i to T_f). The integral is evaluated between two temperature limits, showing that ΔS is also a function of temperature.

Therefore, both ΔS and S are functions of temperature.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A, B and C are three biomolecules. The results of the tests performed on them are given below: A: Molisch's Test Positive, Barfood Test Negative, Biuret Test Negative. B: Molisch's Test Positive, Barfood Test Positive, Biuret Test Negative. C: Molisch's Test Negative, Barfood Test Negative, Biuret Test Positive. A, B and C are respectively:
options: A = Lactose, B = Glucose, C = Alanine
A = Lactose, B = Glucose, C = Albumin
A = Glucose, B = Fructose, C = Albumin
A = Lactose, B = Fructose, C = Alanine
A.sol_text:
To identify the biomolecules, we need to understand what each test detects:

Molisch's Test: Detects carbohydrates (reduces phenol-H2SO4 to give purple ring)
Barfood Test: Detects reducing sugars (aldehyde group present)
Biuret Test: Detects proteins (peptide bonds present)

Analyzing the results:

Compound A: Molisch's Positive, Barfood Negative, Biuret Negative
- Molisch's positive indicates it is a carbohydrate
- Barfood negative indicates it is NOT a reducing sugar
- Therefore, A must be a non-reducing sugar like Lactose

Compound B: Molisch's Positive, Barfood Positive, Biuret Negative
- Molisch's positive indicates it is a carbohydrate
- Barfood positive indicates it is a reducing sugar
- Therefore, B must be a reducing sugar like Glucose

Compound C: Molisch's Negative, Barfood Negative, Biuret Positive
- Molisch's negative indicates it is NOT a carbohydrate
- Biuret positive indicates it is a protein
- Therefore, C must be a protein like Albumin

Thus: A = Lactose, B = Glucose, C = Albumin

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Consider the following reactions, (i) NaNO2/HCl, 0-5°C (ii) β-naphthol/NaOH → Colored Solid; [P] → Br2/H2O → C7H6NBr3. The compound [P] is:
options: NH2 group attached to benzene ring with CH3 group (ortho position)
NH2 group attached to benzene ring with CH3 group (meta position)
NH2 group attached to benzene ring with CH3 group (para position)
NHCH3 group attached to benzene ring with CH3 group (para position)
A.sol_text:
The compound [P] undergoes two different reactions:

1) With NaNO2/HCl at 0-5°C followed by β-naphthol/NaOH → Colored Solid
This is a diazonium coupling reaction. The amine group is converted to diazonium salt (N2+ Cl-) which then couples with β-naphthol to form a colored azo dye.

2) With Br2/H2O → C7H6NBr3
This is an electrophilic aromatic bromination reaction. The product is C7H6NBr3 (three bromines attached).

Analyzing the second reaction:
- Molecular formula C7H6NBr3 indicates:
  - 7 carbons (benzene ring + 1 carbon substituent)
  - 6 hydrogens (benzene ring hydrogens + substituent hydrogens)
  - 1 nitrogen (from amine group)
  - 3 bromines

- The amine group (-NH2) is an activating group and ortho/para directing
- Since 3 bromines are added, they must occupy all available positions ortho and para to the activating -NH2 group
- With a methyl group (-CH3) also present, we need a configuration where:
  - The -NH2 and -CH3 can be positioned such that bromination gives exactly C7H6NBr3
  
- If -NH2 is meta to -CH3 (meta position), bromination at ortho and para positions to -NH2 gives three bromines, which is consistent with the formula

Therefore, [P] is meta-methylaniline (3-methylaniline or m-toluidine): NH2 and CH3 are in meta positions on the benzene ring.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Which of the following reactions will not produce a racemic product?
options: H3C with CH3 attached to a cyclohexene with double bond treated with HCl
A.sol_text:
For a reaction to produce a racemic product, a new chiral center must be formed where there was none before, or an achiral reactant must form a chiral product.

Reaction (1): The cyclohexene with methyl groups undergoes HCl addition. This creates a new chiral center at the carbon where HCl adds. Since the reactant is achiral (or prochiral), addition can occur from both sides equally, producing a racemic mixture.

Reaction (2): CH3CH2CH=CH2 + HBr follows Markovnikov's rule. HBr adds to form CH3CH2CHBr-CH3. The carbon where Br attaches becomes chiral. Since the double bond is not adjacent to an existing chiral center in a way that creates diastereoselectivity, a racemic mixture forms.

Reaction (3): CH3-C(=O)-CH2CH3 + HCN undergoes cyanohydrin formation. A new chiral center is created at the carbonyl carbon. Addition of HCN can occur from both faces of the planar carbonyl group equally, producing a racemic mixture.

Reaction (4): CH3-C(H)(CH3)-CH=CH2 + HCl already contains a chiral center at C-1 (marked with H). When HCl adds to the double bond, it creates a second chiral center. The presence of the existing chiral center directs the addition (via carbocation intermediate) preferentially to one face of the double bond, resulting in diastereomers that are formed unequally. This produces a non-racemic (optically active) product, not a racemic mixture.

Therefore, reaction (4) does NOT produce a racemic product.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Which of the following has the shortest C-Cl bond?
A.sol_text:
The C-Cl bond length depends on the character of the carbon atom bonded to Cl and the electron-withdrawing/donating nature of substituents.

In compound (1) Cl-CH=CH-NO2:
The NO2 group is a strong electron-withdrawing group. It withdraws electron density from the double bond system through resonance and inductive effects. This causes electron density to shift away from the C-Cl bond region, making the Cl-carbon more electron-deficient.

The solution shows resonance structures where the negative charge on nitrogen's oxygen atoms creates a positive charge on the carbon bearing Cl (through resonance with the double bond). This positive character on the carbon increases the electrostatic attraction between C and Cl, shortening the C-Cl bond.

The resonance structures demonstrate:
Cl-CH=CH-N(+)(O(-))O(-) ↔ Cl(+)-CH-CH=N(+)(O(-))O(-) ↔ Cl-CH=CH-N(+)(O(-)2)

The double bond character develops with positive character on carbon adjacent to Cl, which significantly shortens and strengthens the C-Cl bond.

In compounds (2), (3), and (4):
- (2) CH3 is electron-donating (weakly)
- (3) OCH3 is electron-donating (moderately)
- (4) H has minimal effect

These do not have strong electron-withdrawing groups to induce positive character on the C-Cl bearing carbon, so the C-Cl bonds remain longer.

Therefore, compound (1) has the shortest C-Cl bond due to the strong electron-withdrawing NO2 group creating resonance stabilization with positive character on the carbon.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The decreasing order of basicity of the following amines is:
A.sol_text:
To determine the basicity order of amines, we need to consider factors affecting the availability of the lone pair on nitrogen.

Compound (III) - Cyclohexylamine (aliphatic amine):
Nitrogen l.p. not participate in resonance. The lone pair is fully available for donation, making it highly basic.

Compound (I) - Aniline (aromatic primary amine):
Nitrogen l.p. participate in resonance. The lone pair on nitrogen is partially delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance, reducing its availability for protonation. This decreases basicity compared to aliphatic amines.

Compound (II) - Pyridine (aromatic heterocycle):
Nitrogen l.p. participate in resonance and increase the stability of the compound due to aromaticity. The lone pair participates in maintaining the aromatic character, making it less available for protonation. However, pyridine is more basic than aniline because the nitrogen's lone pair is in an sp2 orbital (more electronegative orientation).

Compound (IV) - Pyrrole (aromatic heterocycle):
Nitrogen l.p. participate in resonance due to increase the stability of the compound. The lone pair of nitrogen is essential for the aromaticity of pyrrole (contributes to the 4n+2 pi electrons). The lone pair is heavily involved in resonance, making it least available for protonation. This makes pyrrole the weakest base.

Decreasing order of basicity: (III) > (II) > (I) > (IV)

Note: Aliphatic amines > aromatic amines with conjugated lone pairs > heterocycles with lone pairs in resonance.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The reaction of H3N3B3Cl3(A) with LiBH4 in tetrahydrofuran gives inorganic benzene (B). Further, the reaction of (A) with (C) leads to H3N3B3(Me)3. Compounds (B) and (C) respectively, are :
A.sol_text:
B3N3H3Cl3 + LiBH4 --> B3N3H6 (Inorganic Benzene or Borazine)

The reduction of H3N3B3Cl3 with LiBH4 removes the chlorine atoms and produces borazine (B3N3H6), which is known as inorganic benzene due to its structural similarity to benzene.

B3N3H3Cl + MeMgBr --> B3N3H3(CH3)3 + 3MgBrCl

The reaction of H3N3B3Cl3 with MeMgBr (Grignard reagent) leads to methylation. MeMgBr acts as a nucleophile and replaces the chlorine atoms with methyl groups, producing H3N3B3(Me)3 (or B3N3H3(CH3)3).

Therefore:
Compound (B) = Borazine (product of reduction with LiBH4)
Compound (C) = MeMgBr (Grignard reagent that methylates the compound)

The answer is (4) Borazine and MeMgBr

A.text: In the following reaction A is: A undergoes reaction with (i) Br2, hv (ii) KOH (alc.) (iii) O3 (iv) (CH3)2S (v) NaOH(aq) + Δ to give a product with structure shown as cyclopentanone with an aldehyde group
A.sol_text:
Starting material A undergoes the following transformations:

1) Br2, hv: Radical bromination of A to give brominated product

2) KOH (alc.): Elimination reaction (E2) removes HBr to form an alkene (elimination of HBr from the brominated compound)

3) O3: Ozonolysis of the alkene breaks the double bond

4) (CH3)2S: Reductive workup of the ozonide with dimethyl sulfide gives the carbonyl compound(s)

5) NaOH(aq) + Δ: The dialdehyde undergoes aldol condensation followed by dehydration and intramolecular aldol to form the cyclopentanone with aldehyde side chain shown

Working backwards from the final product (cyclopentanone carboxaldehyde):
- This contains 6 carbons in the main structure
- The ozonolysis must have produced a dialdehyde OHC-(CH2)4-CHO
- Before ozonolysis, this was a double-bonded compound
- The double bond must have been formed by elimination of HBr from a brominated precursor
- Radical bromination of A (a methylcyclopentane) would give the brominated intermediate
- Therefore, A is methylcyclopentane (option 1)

A.text: The isomer (s) of [Co(NH3)4Cl2] that has/have a Cl-Co-Cl angle of 90°, is/are :
A.sol_text:
[Co(NH3)4Cl2]

The complex has octahedral geometry with 4 ammonia ligands and 2 chloride ligands.

For a Cl-Co-Cl angle of 90°, the two chloride ligands must be adjacent (cis arrangement).

In octahedral complexes:
- When two ligands are in cis positions, the angle between them is 90°
- When two ligands are in trans positions, the angle between them is 180°

Possible isomers of [Co(NH3)4Cl2]:
1. cis isomer: The two Cl ligands occupy adjacent positions → Cl-Co-Cl angle = 90° ✓
2. trans isomer: The two Cl ligands occupy opposite positions → Cl-Co-Cl angle = 180° ✗

Therefore, only the cis isomer has a Cl-Co-Cl angle of 90°.

Answer: cis only

Dichromate = Cr2O7^(2-)

B.text: A sample of milk splits after 60 min. at 300 K and after 40 min. at 400 K when the population of lactobacillus acidophilus in it doubles. The activation energy (in kJ/mol) for this process is closest to ____ (Given, R = 8.3 J mol^(-1) K^(-1), ln(2/3) = 0.4, e^(-3) = 4.0)
B.sol_text:
Using the Arrhenius equation in the form:
ln(K2/K1) = (Ea/R)[1/T1 - 1/T2]

Since the population doubles, K2/K1 represents the ratio of rate constants at the two temperatures.

At 300 K, population doubles in 60 min.
At 400 K, population doubles in 40 min.

ln(60/40) = (Ea/8.3)[1/300 - 1/400]

ln(1.5) = (Ea/8.3)[1/300 - 1/400]

1/300 - 1/400 = (4 - 3)/(1200) = 1/1200

ln(60/40) = (Ea/8.3) × (1/1200)

Ea = 3.98 kJ/mole

A.text: If z be a complex number satisfying |Re(z)| + |Im(z)| = 4, then |z| cannot be -

given that |Re(z)| + |Im(z)| = 4
∴ |x| + |y| = 4

The constraint |x| + |y| = 4 represents a diamond (square rotated 45°) with vertices at A(4, 0), B(0, 4), C(-4, 0), and D(0, -4).

Maximum value of |z| = 4
This occurs at the vertices where |z| = sqrt(4^2 + 0^2) = 4 or |z| = sqrt(0^2 + 4^2) = 4

Or: x + y - 4 = 0

1 = x + 1/y

The following system of linear equations

A.text: If one end of a focal chord AB of the parabola y^2 = 8x is at A(1/2, -2), then the equation of the tangent to it at B is -
A.sol_text:
y^2 = 8x (a = 2)

Let one end of focal chord is (at^2, 2at) = (1/2, -2)

=> 2at = -2
=> t = -1/2

other end of focal chord will be (a/t^2, -2a/t) ≡ (8, 8)

Now, tangent at B(8, 8)

=> y(8) = 8((x + 8)/2)

=> x - 2y + 8 = 0

A.text: Let f and g be differentiable functions on R such that fog is the identity function. If for some a, b ∈ R, g'(a) = 5 and g(a) = b, then f'(b) is equal to -
A.sol_text:
fog is an identity function
∴ fog(x) = x

Differentiating both sides with respect to x:
f'(g(x)); g'(x) = 1

Put x = a
⇒ f'(g(a)); g'(a) = 1
⇒ f'(b) (5) = 1
⇒ f'(b) = 1/5

B.text: If the distance between the plane 23x - 10y - 2z + 48 = 0 and the plane containing the lines (x+1)/2 = (y-3)/4 = (z+1)/3 and (x+3)/2 = (y+2)/6 = (z-1)/lambda (lambda ∈ R) is equal to k/sqrt(633), then k is equal to ___.
B.sol_text:
Required distance = perpendicular distance of plane 23x - 10y - 2z + 48 = 0 either from (-1, 3, -1) or (-3, -2, 1)

=> |(-23 - 30 + 2 + 48)|/sqrt((23)^2 + (10)^2 + (2)^2) = k/sqrt(633)

=> 3/sqrt(633) = k/sqrt(633)

∴ k = 3

B.text: The number of terms common to the two A.P.'s 3, 7, 11, ..... 407 and 2, 9, 16, .... 709 is ________.
B.sol_text:
First A.P. is 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, ..... 407
Second A.P. is 2, 9, 16, 23, ..... 709

First common term = 23
Common difference d = L.C.M. (4, 7) = 28

Last term ≤ 407
=> 23 + (n - 1)(28) ≤ 407
=> n ≤ 14.7

So, n = 14

B.text: If the curves, x^2 - 6x + y^2 + 8 = 0 and x^2 - 8y + y^2 + 16 - k = 0, (k > 0) touch each other at a point, then the largest value of k is ___.
B.sol_text:
C1 = (3, 0), C2 = (0, 4)

r1 = sqrt(9 + 0 - 8) = 1; r2 = sqrt(16 - 16 + k) = sqrt(k)

Two circles touch each other
∴ C1C2 = |r1 + r2|

5 = |1 + sqrt(k)|

⇒ 1 + sqrt(k) = 5 or sqrt(k) - 1 = 5

⇒ k = 16 or k = 36

Maximum value of k = 36
